Definition: Is the register integrated with the national ID system?
Comments: World Bank ID4D notes since 2008 birth registrations require entry of parents' national ID numbers, creating a linkage/feedback loop with the national ID system, but not fully automatic real-time integration.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Kenya's Maisha Namba/Unique Personal Identifier is assigned at birth registration and becomes the national ID number at age 18 (ID4Africa 2024 country profile); government plans (Feb 2025) to automate ID issuance from civil registry data at 18. However the digital ID rollout remains at pilot stage with implementation delays and legal challenges (Center for Financial Inclusion, Aug 2024), so "Partially integrated" (4) still fits better than full integration.

Definition: Are all non-citizens allowed to be included in the register?
Comments: Kenya's Civil Registration Services information states births and deaths registration is compulsory for all events occurring in Kenya regardless of nationality, implying inclusion of non-citizens.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. eCitizen's Civil Registration Services page states registration of births/deaths is compulsory for all events in Kenya "without regard to nationality"; UNHCR Kenya confirms refugees at Kakuma/Kalobeyei receive birth and death certificates through the Civil Registrar, and a Plan International field handbook confirms registration is free of charge for Kenyan nationals, non-citizens and refugees alike. Supports "All included".

Definition: Does the register cover births, deaths and marriages?
Comments: UN CRVSID case study indicates civil registration system covers births and deaths, while marriages/divorces are managed under separate justice/Attorney General systems, so digital civil register scope is partial.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed from 2 to 3. The 2023 UN CRVSID case study notes marriages sit under a separate Attorney-General system, but that does not mean the process is non-digital: marriage notice, licensing and certificate issuance are processed online via eCitizen, and as of January 2026 the Registrar of Marriages ended manual certificate printing entirely in favour of digital-only issuance. Combined with existing digital birth/death registration (and a May 2026 digital birth-notification rollout), all three vital-event types are now captured digitally, even though births/deaths and marriages sit on separate agency platforms (CRS vs Registrar of Marriages).

Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
Comments: Reported birth registration around 70% (Kenya Civil Registration & Vital Statistics report referenced by The Star social post) and death registration around mid-40s; using birth registration completeness as proxy places Kenya in 70–89% category.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed, replacing the weak Facebook-post source with authoritative data. A peer-reviewed DHS-based study (PMC, 2025/26) puts national birth registration coverage at 76.0% in 2022 (up from 69.0% in 2014); the UN CRVSID paper cites 86% for 2021 (Annual Vital Statistics Report, CRS); KNBS's own 2023 Vital Statistics Report provides the underlying administrative data. Both independent estimates fall within the 70–89% band, confirming Value Code 4.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the national ID system?
Comments: World Bank ID4D diagnostic describes IPRS pulling data from the National Registration Bureau (national ID) and being used widely to validate national ID credentials, indicating strong operational integration with national ID.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with fresher sources. Kenya's IPRS (population register) integrates National ID, birth/death, foreign-national and refugee data into one database (ID4Africa 2024 country profile) and has for over a decade let telecoms and financial institutions verify identity remotely by querying the database against the national ID (Center for Financial Inclusion, Aug 2024). This is longstanding, nationwide, operational integration, supporting "Fully integrated nationwide", though the transition to the new Maisha Namba configuration is a risk to monitor going forward.

Definition: Does the government maintain one or more social protection registers?
Comments: Kenya's National Social Protection Secretariat operates the Enhanced Single Registry (ESR), a web-based socio-economic database of vulnerable households linking multiple social protection programmes, indicating a fully operational social protection registry.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with stronger, more recent evidence. Official KSEIP2 operations guidelines (Nov 2025) state the ESR "serves as Kenya's centralised database of poor and vulnerable households across all 47 counties"; an independent academic paper (SSOAR, Jan 2026) confirms data collection from all 47 counties was completed by December 2024, covering roughly 4.9 million households. This supports "Fully deployed nationwide".

Definition: Is the register integrated with the national ID system?
Comments: NSPS describes beneficiary details being verified electronically against the National Population Registry (IPRS) database to prevent fraud/double dipping, indicating partial integration with national ID/population identity systems.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The NSPS Single Registry page states the registry "is linked to the Integrated Population Registration System (IPRS), so that programme beneficiaries can be authenticated by their national ID numbers," and the 2024 Social Protection Bill codifies electronic verification of beneficiaries against relevant registries. Integration is not universal (e.g. child beneficiaries without a national ID are verified via birth certificates instead), so "Partially integrated" remains the accurate code.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the national ID system?
Comments: KRA PIN registration processes require national identification documents for individuals and Alien ID for non-citizens, indicating operational linkage to national ID/identity documents though not necessarily full system integration.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed, with evidence now going beyond a mere document requirement (the original source cited a business-registration page, not individual PIN registration). KRA's individual PIN registration requirements page confirms National ID/Alien ID details are required, and third-party API documentation shows IPRS exposes a live "KRA PIN by ID number" lookup while KRA's own GavaConnect checker API offers a PIN-by-ID-number endpoint, evidencing genuine system-level (API) linkage between tax and national ID records. PIN and ID remain distinct identifiers rather than a single unified number, so "Partially integrated" still fits.
